Family mill · New Paris, Ohio
Seventy years of feed, grain, and neighbors.
Riegel Feed & Grain has stood on North Washington Street since 1954. We custom grind and mix feed, buy and sell grain, and keep a working store for livestock, pets, show animals, and the family freezer.

What we do
A mill, an elevator, and a store that still carries “a little bit of everything.”
That line is how owner Nicole Wood describes the place — custom grind and mix, grain, mulch and landscaping, show supplies, farm-fresh beef and pork, dog and cat food, and the everyday goods a farm town actually uses.
Custom grind & mix
Bring your grain or start from ours. We grind and mix livestock rations to order.
Buy & sell grain
Licensed Ohio grain warehouse. Call for bids, dump hours, and harvest updates.
Farm-fresh beef & pork
Meat for the family table, sold from the mill store. Ask what is in this week.
Pets, mulch & show
Dog and cat food, landscaping mulch, show supplies, and animal health products.
Since 1954
Grandpa started it. The family still runs it.
Vaughn D. Riegel opened the mill in the spring of 1954. He was a cattleman, farmer, and U.S. Army veteran who lived the rest of his life in New Paris. He retired as owner-operator in 2008. The mill is now run by his son Dwight Riegel and granddaughter Nicole Wood, with Nicole’s brother — three generations on the same street.
The corporation was organized in Ohio in 1996. The mill itself is older than that: a working country elevator that still custom-grinds feed and still knows the farms around Preble County by name.
Read the family story
“Grandpa started this in 1954. We custom grind and mix feed. We buy and sell grain. We have mulch and landscaping supplies, show supplies, a little bit of everything.”
Nicole Wood, owner · Preble County Local Business Spotlight, 2025
The store
Come in for feed. Leave with supper.
Visit Preble County lists us for farm-fresh beef and pork, livestock feed, dog and cat food, and more. Ohio’s tourism listing notes seed cleaning, feed grinding, animal health products, and meat in the general store.
